If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, inflate early forecast by 1.5–2.0% to capture bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, deflate early forecast by 1.5–2.0% to avoid overconfidence in bearish trends.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in mid-period (days 10–15), adjust forecast upward by 0.8–1.2% to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.  
If sentiment drops to 0.00 in mid-period, reduce forecast by 0.8–1.2% to reflect risk-off behavior.  
In late forecast (days 25–30), if sentiment remains flat (0.33–0.67), apply no correction — true path often stabilizes near prior range.  
If sentiment is 1.00 in late forecast, add 0.5–1.0% to final day to capture sentiment-driven breakout potential.
